patients.label: 75-year-old woman with memory complaints diagnosed with mild Alzheimer’s dementia and advised on driving

identity_evidence.quote: 75-year-old female patient, consulted our Memory Clinic in 2015

attribution_limitations: The alcohol history is called unclear by the authors: the patient reports stopping relevant drinking four months ago and recently drinking one glass of beer per week, the partner never noticed increased consumption, and the daughter suggests regular consumption with unclear amounts. Third-party accounts are contradictory and unsubstantiated.

The CSF beta-amyloid 1–42 value (849 pg/mL) is called normal while the printed cut-off reads ≤450 pg/mL; the cut-off direction as printed does not match a normal value. The text then states the neurodegeneration markers were pathological without classifying total tau and phosphorylated tau individually.

Two different time frames are given for the neuropsychologist’s advice to refrain from driving: until the next consultation with the physician, and (in the discussion) until the more complete work-up would provide a definite diagnosis.

The authors give an alternative explanation for the wrong-way driving event (stress before the visit) but chose to interpret it as decompensation under underlying cognitive disability. The event itself was relayed by a caller to the daughter.

The authors’ first-consultation summary lists slight subjective orientation difficulties, whereas the patient history states she did not report difficulties with spatial orientation. These are different wordings (general orientation vs spatial orientation) and are not treated as a source conflict.
The statement that the authors opted to wait is an answer to a rhetorical either/or question, while another paragraph says driving safety was brought up at this stage in a preliminary manner.
The authors propose a cholinesterase inhibitor and report that the patient was willing to be medicated; no drug name, start or administration is reported.

The text says the clinic does not routinely perform hippocampal volumetry; it does not state whether it was done for this patient. Generic workflow statements and general advice to drivers (second opinion at driving schools or road safety agencies, insurance cover) are not assigned to this patient.

Table 1 prints the z-Score of the digit-span row with a decimal comma (0,1), lists a VLMT–D1 word span test that the methods text does not describe, and uses words (impaired, not impaired, normal mood, slightly depressive) in the z-Score column of some rows. The VLMT–D1 row prints the same raw score and z-Score (3, −1.3) as the RAVLT trial 1 row; the two rows are kept separate as printed.

The speaker of the outcome sentences changes between the case narrative and the discussion; discussion sentences naming the patient or Mrs. L. were assigned to the single index patient, while generic discussion sentences were not.

Several course steps have no literal order: the social worker home visit "three weeks later" is separated from the rescheduled advice by two generic sentences; "After all, diagnostic information was available" is punctuated as "After all," and names no test, so it does not order the neuropsychological examination, MRI or CSF analysis before the formal diagnosis; and the discussion sentence "Latter results especially prompted us to advise" is not identified as the neuropsychologist advice event.

limitations: The article has no figures and no supplements; no visual, figure-EHR privacy content or supplement review applies.
Table 1 is a single-time neuropsychological result table, not a serial table; each row is one observation with its raw score and z-Score column text, units only where the source prints them.
Third-party accounts (partner, daughter, caller) are contradictory or hearsay and are recorded with that provenance; alcohol facts from third parties are review_only.
Cohort, literature and policy statements in the introduction and discussion are not assigned to the patient.
No medication was started for the dementia: a cholinesterase inhibitor was only proposed.
